title: Twenty who are steadfast can overcome two hundred.
subtitle: Patience multiplies a small number
then: At Badr the Prophet ﷺ told his Companions: {reward}rise toward a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth.{/reward} Umayr bin Al-Humam said, excellent, excellent, hoping to be among its people. The verse promised that {idea}twenty who were steadfast would overcome two hundred.{/idea}
now: You are the only one in your office who prays. The only one in your family trying to quit smoking. The few volunteers keeping the food bank open. {idea}Being few is not the same as being weak.{/idea} Steady, patient people carry far more than their number.
old: There are too few of us to make a difference.
new: A few patient, steady people can do what crowds cannot.
try: Find one other person working toward the same good as you, and encourage them today.

title: Now Allah has lightened it, knowing there is weakness in you.
subtitle: A load adjusted to what people can bear
then: Ibn Abbas said the earlier ratio {trap}became difficult for the Muslims.{/trap} Then came this verse: {reward}now Allah has lightened it for you, for He knows there is weakness in you.{/reward} The load was eased to match what they could carry, and the verse ends: Allah is with the patient.
now: You set yourself a plan: pray every night, read a juz a day, never lose your temper. You fell short and want to give up entirely. {idea}Allah knows your weakness and still asks for what you can do.{/idea} Lighten the plan, don't drop it.
old: If I can't do the full amount, there's no point.
new: Allah knows my weakness. A smaller, steady amount is still welcome.
try: Take one goal you've been failing at. Cut it to a size you can actually keep, and start today.

title: You want this world's gain. Allah wants the Hereafter for you.
subtitle: The question of the captives at Badr
then: After Badr the Prophet ﷺ asked his Companions about the captives, saying {idea}only yesterday they were your brothers.{/idea} Umar advised one course, Abu Bakr advised pardon in exchange for ransom, and the Prophet ﷺ accepted ransom. The verse came: {trap}you desire the goods of this world,{/trap} {idea}but Allah desires the Hereafter.{/idea}
now: A decision at work: the option that pays more now, or the one you'd be proud of before Allah. The weekend: the extra shift, or the visit to your aging mother. {idea}Ask which want is leading.{/idea}
old: Taking the gain in front of me is just being practical.
new: Allah wants the lasting good for me. I can let that lead my choices.
try: In one choice today, ask which option you'd prefer on the Day you meet Allah, and pick it.

title: Were it not for a prior decree from Allah.
subtitle: Mercy that was written before the mistake
then: Ibn Abbas and many others explained the prior decree as {reward}Allah having already written that spoils would be made lawful for this community.{/reward} Without it, {trap}a great punishment would have touched them for what they took.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said he was given things no prophet before him was given.
now: You look back at a decision that could have gone badly: the drive home tired, the investment you didn't check, the words you almost said. {reward}You were spared before you knew you needed it.{/reward} That is mercy written ahead of time.
old: It turned out fine, so I must have been right.
new: Sometimes I was spared not because I was right, but because Allah's mercy came first.
try: Recall a close call in your life. Thank Allah today for the mercy you didn't see at the time.

title: Enjoy what is lawful and good, and keep mindful of Allah.
subtitle: After the warning, permission and forgiveness

key.label: How to hold what is lawful

then: After the stern words of the last two verses, Allah tells them {reward}to eat of what they had gained, lawful and good,{/reward} and {idea}to stay mindful of Him.{/idea} Abu Hurayrah said this is because spoils had never been made lawful for anyone before them. The verse ends: Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
now: You earned your salary honestly, and still feel strange enjoying it. Or you enjoy it so much you forget who gave it. {idea}The verse finds the middle.{/idea} Enjoy what is lawful, gratefully, with Allah in mind.
old: Enjoying good things feels a bit unspiritual.
new: Enjoying the lawful with gratitude and taqwa is what Allah invites.
try: Enjoy one good, lawful thing today slowly, and thank Allah for it out loud.

title: If there is good in your hearts, He will give you better.
subtitle: Hope offered to the captives
then: Al-Abbas, the Prophet's ﷺ uncle, was among the captives and had to pay ransom. Ibn Kathir reports that {trap}he lost twenty uwqiyah,{/trap} and later said: {reward}after I became Muslim, Allah gave me twenty servants in their place, and I hope for His forgiveness.{/reward} The night after Badr, the Prophet ﷺ could not sleep until his uncle's bonds were loosened.
now: The job you lost, the money that disappeared in a bad deal, the plan that fell through. {reward}Allah looks at your heart, not just your account.{/reward} If there is good there, what He gives in return can be better than what was taken.
old: What I lost is gone. Nothing can replace it.
new: If Allah finds good in my heart, He can give me better than what I lost.
try: Think of one recent loss. Ask Allah sincerely to replace it with something better.

title: If they plan to betray you, Allah already knows.
subtitle: Words said and what is in the heart
then: Ibn Kathir explains: if they intend to betray you, {trap}contrary to what they declare in words,{/trap} they already betrayed Allah before Badr. {idea}Allah knows what they do and is Wise in what He decides.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ was not asked to read hearts.
now: You suspect someone's kindness is fake: the in-law, the coworker, the new friend. You replay their words, hunting for the trick. {idea}You are not asked to read hearts.{/idea} Act fairly on what you see, and leave the rest to the All-Knowing.
old: I need to figure out what everyone is really thinking.
new: I deal with what I can see. Allah knows what is hidden.
try: Next time you catch yourself guessing someone's hidden motive, stop and give them the benefit of the doubt.

title: Those who left everything and those who took them in.
subtitle: The Muhajirin and the Ansar, allies to one another

row.title: allies
sub: each more right to the other

then: The Muhajirin {idea}left their homes and estates for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.{/idea} The Ansar of Madinah {reward}took them into their own homes and shared their wealth.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ paired them as brothers. The verse also tells them to help believers far away who ask for aid, {idea}without breaking any treaty they had made.{/idea}
now: The family that just arrived in your city knowing no one. The student far from home during Ramadan. The colleague who moved here alone. {idea}You can be someone's Ansar.{/idea} A meal, a lift, a spare room for a week.
old: Newcomers will find their own way. It's not my responsibility.
new: Taking in those who left home is how strangers become brothers and sisters.
try: Invite someone new to your area, or far from family, for a meal this week.

title: If you do not stand by one another, corruption spreads.
subtitle: What happens when the good stop supporting each other
then: After describing the bond among believers, the verse notes that {trap}those who opposed them supported one another.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that if the believers {idea}did not stay loyal to each other,{/idea} confusion and widespread trial would follow. The concern was the community holding together in that early time.
now: The honest colleague who gets isolated while the cliquey ones protect each other. The friend trying to stay sober who gets no backup. {idea}People doing wrong often stick together. People doing right often leave each other alone.{/idea} Be the support.
old: As long as I'm doing good myself, that's enough.
new: Good people need to stand by each other, or wrong fills the gap.
try: Message one person who is trying to do the right thing and tell them you're with them.

title: They are the believers in truth.
subtitle: The surah ends where it began

row.title: love and follow them
sub: a person is with whom he loves

then: Ibn Kathir notes the surah {idea}affirms their faith just as at its beginning,{/idea} echoing 8:4: these are the believers in truth. The Prophet ﷺ said, in a hadith with many chains: {reward}a person will be with those he loves.{/reward}
now: You weren't at Badr. You didn't leave Makkah or open your home in Madinah. {reward}You can still love them and walk their way.{/reward} Read about them, give like the Ansar, hold firm like the Muhajirin, in the small daily ways your life allows.
old: The best generation is gone. I can only admire them from far away.
new: Loving them and following their way, I can hope to be with them.
try: Read one short story about a Companion today and copy one thing they did.

title: Those who came later and strove with you are of you.
subtitle: Late arrivals belong, and family ties keep their right

row.title: too late to belong
sub: the first ones got it all

then: The surah ends by welcoming {idea}those who believed afterward, emigrated, and strove alongside the first believers: they are of you.{/idea} It then states that {reward}relatives by blood are nearer to one another in Allah's decree,{/reward} which Ibn Abbas and others said replaced the early inheritance between paired brothers.
now: You came to practice late: after years away, after university, after your first child. You feel like you missed the start. {idea}The verse says: you are of them.{/idea} And while you embrace your new brothers and sisters, don't neglect your own family.
old: I came to faith too late to really belong.
new: Those who come later and strive are fully counted. And my family still has its right.
try: Call one relative you've drifted from today, and welcome one newcomer at the mosque this week.
